reviewer_notes: Paper builds one ML methodology (multiple linear regression) with five separate section-level energy-consumption equations (reforming fuel gas M1, reforming steam M2, package boiler fuel gas M3, synthesis gas compressor HP steam M4, air compressor MP steam M5), all fitted on Aspen Hysys simulation data (3876 rows per SEU, 80/20 train-test split) and validated against four actual plants (A-D). M6 captures the plant-level SEC (MMBtu/ton NH3) intensity ratio used as EnPI and where the energy/cost/CO2 savings are reported. The four actual plants are treated as one multi-site application because the same models are applied across all of them. R Square values (Table 4) recorded as in-sample fit; ML-vs-actual deviation percentages (Table 5) as out-of-sample validation. Estimation method OLS inferred from scikit-learn LinearRegression (not explicitly named). Ammonia classified as continuous chemical production, not petrochemical. K1 (validity envelope) is a soft inference from the SOE bounding of the model/training data; reviewer to confirm.
